candidates.explanation: The authentication service directly obtains an operational authentication-state manager through its shared singleton rather than an explicit, replaceable dependency.
candidates.title: Direct Singleton Service Access

evidence.description: The class exposes a global access path through its public static shared instance.
The shared instance contains mutable tokens, SSO credentials, login status, user profile, and a user-info-fetch flag.
setupTokensWithCredentials writes the instance's tokens and login status without synchronization or actor isolation.

candidates.explanation: Mutable authentication state is reachable through the public shared instance without visible actor isolation or synchronization.
candidates.title: Shared Mutable Instance State Without Isolation

evidence.description: EcosiaAuthenticationService is declared as a class without Sendable conformance or actor isolation.
The class visibly contains mutable instance state, including userProfile and skipUserInfoFetch.
setupTokensWithCredentials starts a Task that captures the service through its instance-method call to dispatchAuthStateChange.
After setupTokensWithCredentials starts that task, login continues reading skipUserInfoFetch and invoking fetchUserInfoFromAuth0 on the same service.
The subsequent fetch operation mutates userProfile on the same captured service instance.

candidates.explanation: The mutable, non-Sendable authentication-service instance is captured by an unstructured task while the initiating operation continues accessing that same instance. No ownership transfer or isolation boundary prevents conflicting access.
candidates.title: Non-Sendable Value Crossing an Isolation Boundary
